Where it began

Jos Buttler was born in Taunton on 8 September 1990 and went to King's College in the town, where his runs filled the school record books. In one 50-over schools match in 2008 he made 227 not out and shared an opening stand of 340. Two years later he was named the Young Wisden Schools Cricketer of the Year.

He came up through Somerset's age-group teams and made his first-class debut for the county in 2009. Before he turned 20 he was winning matches for them with quick, inventive runs. He later moved north to Lancashire, keen to keep wicket every week.

The player

Buttler played 57 Tests for England between 2014 and 2022, scoring 2,907 runs at 31.95 with two hundreds and 18 fifties. Behind the stumps he held 130 catches and made one stumping, and he took 23 more catches in the field. He made 85 in his first Test innings, against India, and his first Test hundred, 106, came against the same opponents in 2018. His best, 152 at Southampton in 2020, was a long and patient innings that showed another side of him.

In white-ball cricket he was one of the most exciting batters of his time. He was in the side that won the 2019 World Cup, making 59 in the final and then completing the run out in the super over that settled it. Three years later, as captain, he led England to the T20 World Cup.

What made him special

Buttler could hit the ball to places other batters had not thought of. He scooped and ramped it over the keeper, reversed it, and swivelled to send it fine, yet the hitting was clean rather than wild. When a run chase needed calm hands, he often had them.

The longer game asked him to be more patient, and he worked hard at it. His Southampton hundred took 311 balls, which for him must have felt like a week. There were days when the gloves gave him more trouble than the bat, but he kept turning up and putting in the work.

Away from the middle

He became one of the most sought-after players in franchise cricket, with spells in Australia, Bangladesh, South Africa and England, and his best years in the IPL came with Rajasthan Royals. In 2022 he made four hundreds in a single IPL season. In August 2026 he passed Kieron Pollard to become the leading run-scorer in men's T20 cricket.

He was made an MBE in the 2020 New Year Honours and was named a Wisden Cricketer of the Year. He follows Manchester City.

And finally

The most famous moment of his career did not involve a bat at all. It was a wide throw, a quick gather and the bails whipped off, and it won England a World Cup. The BBC later named it their moment of the year, which is quite a reward for tidying up somebody else's throw.
